annotations.title: Save structured fields extracted from papers

description: Save a structured extraction (named fields with values, such as sample_size, method, country, outcome) for one or many papers, as a child note on each paper: a readable table plus a machine-readable copy, tagged "zoteus-extraction". Zotero has no custom fields; a note syncs and anyone can read it in Zotero. YOU read the paper (zotero_get_fulltext) and supply the values: this server has no language model. Give each value the verbatim `quote` it rests on, and its `page`: when the paper's full text is available (Zotero's index, or the PDF or EPUB itself) the quote is checked against it and the verdict ("verified", "not-found" or "unchecked", with the page it was found on when known) is stored beside the value. A quote that was not found is still saved, and named in the result, so you can correct it. `schema` names the extraction (e.g. "rct-review"): one note per paper and schema. Saving again for the same paper and schema UPDATES that note in place: fields you send replace fields of the same name, a null value removes a field, fields you do not mention are kept (pass `replace_all:true` to drop them), and the result lists every replaced and removed value with what it was. Nothing else in the library is touched. Read the extractions back as one table with zotero_extraction_table. Writes go to the running Zotero desktop app (Zotero 10+) for every library it holds, otherwise to the cloud Web API.

items.description: One entry per paper, at most 50.

fields.description: The fields extracted from this paper.

name.description: Field name, e.g. "sample_size", "method", "country". The same name across papers makes one column.

page.description: Page of the quote, as you read it (e.g. "4" or "4-5").

quote.description: Verbatim passage the value rests on. Checked against the item's full text when there is one, and the verdict is stored.

value.description: The value you read from the paper. null removes the field from the saved extraction.

item_key.description: 8-character key of the paper (a regular item, not its PDF).

library_id.description: Numeric id of the library to address, e.g. 5234875 for a group (zotero_groups lists the ids you can reach). Omit to use the configured default library; an id given without library_type is read as a group id.

library_type.description: Which library to address: "user" (a personal library) or "group" (a shared group library). Omit to use the library this server is configured for. "group" on its own is refused: pass library_id with it.

replace_all.description: Drop fields already saved for a paper that this call does not mention (default false: they are kept).

schema.description: Name of the extraction schema, e.g. "rct-review". Papers saved under the same name form one table.

verify_quotes.description: Check each quote against the paper's full text (default true). Off skips reading the text and stores quotes as "unchecked".

name: zotero_save_extraction

items.description: One entry per paper, in the order given.

added.description: Fields that were not in the note before.

duplicates.description: Other extraction notes for the same paper and schema, left as they are.

kept.description: Fields already in the note that this call left as they were.

notFound.description: Fields whose quote was not found in the full text.

quotes.description: How the quotes sent in this call fared.

notFound.description: Quotes NOT found in the full text that was checked.

unchecked.description: Quotes that could not be checked (no full text, too short, or verification off).

verified.description: Quotes found in the full text.

removed.description: Fields removed from the note, by a null value or by replace_all.

replaced.description: Fields whose saved entry this call replaced, with the value it held.

saved.description: Papers whose note was created or updated.

target.description: Where the write went: "local" (Zotero desktop local API), "desktop" (connector protocol) or "cloud" (Zotero Web API).

title: Save structured fields extracted from papers
